articles.title: Boston Celtics’ Neemias Queta Opens Up on Fighting for Minutes With Mitchell Robinson
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics added Mitchell Robinson to their ranks to beef up their frontcourt depth this offseason, and Neemias Queta recently weighed in on how he’l...
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics added Mitchell Robinson to their ranks to beef up their frontcourt depth this offseason, and Neemias Queta recently weighed in on how he'll mesh with the former No. 36 pick this upcoming season.

After establishing himself as the Boston Celtics ' starting center this past season, Queta signed a four-year, $56 million contract extension. But with Robinson's arrival, it remains to be seen how he'll keep his starting job and minutes.

"I'm not too worried about that. That's a Joe (Mazzulla) to figure out," Queta told Celtics on CLNS. "I'm out there just welcoming my new teammate with open arms. Mitchell's going to be a great addition for us. I'm extremely happy I don't have to go against him anymore because he used to get all these rebounds."

"It's going to be good to have him on our side, being able to have a player that's so accomplished — being able to guard multiple positions. One of the best rebounders the league has ever seen. So, nothing but welcome with open arms for him. And I'm excited to be his teammate," he added.

Boston Celtics News: Neemias Queta shares what he has been up to this offseason

In the same interview, Neemias Queta said he has spent the summer sharpening his game on both ends of the floor, which has been evident while playing for Portugal in the FIBA World Cup qualifiers .

"I've been working on different facets of the game, being more versatile. Offensively, being more complete, whether it's making quick decisions with the ball or there's a pass, being able to go and get my own shot, and defensively; being able to be in the right spots earlier," Queta said.

"And communicate a little bit more. The same old stuff; the space on the floor, as well. Being able to shoot. It's just been a good offseason to work, and I've been working on pretty much everything," he added.

The 27-year-old center is coming off a career year in 2025-26, averaging 10.2 points, 8.4 rebounds, 1.7 assists, and 1.3 blocks on 65.3 percent shooting from the field across 76 regular-season appearances for the Boston Celtics.

articles.title: Lavezzi opens up on post-retirement depression and Messi support
articles.summary: Former Argentina forward Ezequiel Lavezzi has opened up on how close friend Lionel Messi helped him through depression and the "void" of life after retiremen...
articles.body:
Former Argentina forward Ezequiel Lavezzi has opened up on how close friend Lionel Messi helped him through depression and the "void" of life after retirement.

Lavezzi enjoyed successful spells at Napoli and Paris Saint-Germain as well as helping Argentina reach the 2014 World Cup final, where they were beaten 1-0 by Germany after extra time.

The 41-year-old finished his playing career in November 2019 after a spell at Hebei China Fortune.

Lavezzi revealed in an interview with Amazon Prime Italia how he had struggled to adapt after hanging up his boots, but also focused on the close bonds with former team-mates which helped him through tough times and on towards recovery.

"When I stopped playing, there was a void, and there was nothing to fill it," Lavezzi said.

"I struggled with depression, I was hospitalised. I am taking medication and undergoing treatment, and I am slowly recovering.

"The arrival of my son changed my life, he brings me so much joy and makes me feel alive. He gave me the strength to keep going."

Lavezzi added: "To those who suffer, I say that with humility and desire, you can overcome it. The world of football has been very close to me, so many have been close to me, like Messi, (Sergio) Aguero , Paolo Cannavaro .

"I have a special friendship with Messi, we talk about many things, he is a fantastic person."

articles.title: Ian Wright reveals incredible Mark Viduka Celtic dressing-room walkout in Inverness disaster
articles.summary: Ian Wright has recalled the remarkable moment Mark Viduka refused to return for the second half of Celtic’s infamous Scottish Cup defeat to Inverness Caledon...
articles.body:
Ian Wright has recalled the remarkable moment Mark Viduka refused to return for the second half of Celtic's infamous Scottish Cup defeat to Inverness Caledonian Thistle.

The 3-1 loss at Celtic Park in February 2000 ultimately cost John Barnes his job, but Wright has revealed the turmoil had already begun inside the dressing room at half-time.

Speaking on The Green Room, the former Celtic striker recalled Viduka beginning to remove his kit as Barnes and assistant Eric Black questioned what he was doing.

Wright said via The Overlap: "Yeah, Inverness Caledonian Thistle. He [Viduka] just started taking his gear off. I've never seen it before.

"You know, we're losing obviously Caledonian Thistle and came halftime the fans are booing, going crazy.

"He just came in and you know when someone just like the end of the game you start taking your gear off. Started taking his gear off and Barnes and Eric Black said what you doing?

"He says, 'F*** this man. I've had enough of this.'"

Wright claims Viduka then headed for the shower, leaving Barnes needing to make an unexpected half-time substitution.

Wright continued: "When they were talking to him and he just went into the shower and then Barnes went, 'Wright', I go for f*** sake, 'Wright get stripped, he's not coming back, you're a disgrace.'

"But it was like one of those when you're watching it in real time, it's like a film. You can't believe what you're seeing."

Viduka's absence was attributed to a knee injury by his agent at the time, while reports also suggested there had been a dressing-room confrontation involving the Australian and Black.

Roy Keane, who was listening to Wright recount the incident, admitted he could understand a player reaching breaking point mentally, although he stressed Viduka's actions were wrong.

Keane said: "That's not right but also when a player's mindset when your head goes…"

Keane replied: "No, I get that, of course I'm saying it's not right. But also, a player, when your head's gone, the head's gone, isn't it?"

Wright then said: "He went to the point of no return."

Celtic were actually trailing 2-1 at the interval rather than 1-0, with Wright replacing Viduka for the second half.

There was to be no comeback as Inverness completed a stunning 3-1 victory at Parkhead. Barnes was dismissed just two days later, bringing his ill-fated spell as Celtic manager to an end.

articles.title: Southend boss Dyer pledges to keep attacking style
articles.summary: Southend United boss Kieron Dyer urges fans not to get too giddy yet, but says they will maintain their attacking style.
articles.body:
Southend United boss Kieron Dyer says fans cannot get too giddy with their fine start but has promised to keep playing attacking football.

The Shrimpers go into Tuesday's National League game at home to Tamworth fifth in the table, three points behind early leaders Boreham Wood.

Southend have won four of their opening seven league matches under new boss Dyer who is in his first managerial role following a glittering career at Ipswich Town, Newcastle United and with England.

"In the worst possible way, winning three games to start off was a bad kind of thing because everybody gets a bit giddy and 'we're going to win the league'," the 47-year-old told BBC Radio Essex.

"I want everyone to think we have a great chance to win the league, but you've got to remember we are a really new team, with new coaching staff and new ways of playing.

"We've got to be really happy with our players and how quickly they've adjusted and got points on the board."

Dyer is already bringing his attacking playing style to the way he is setting up the Shrimpers, who lost in the play-offs in 2025-2026.

They've scored 14 goals in seven matches, taking six points from a possible nine at Roots Hall.

"We have to make this place a fortress. We had the set-back against Kidderminster , but our three performances at home have been of a good, high quality - with control and exciting football.

"Again, I want us to be really positive. I'm going to put as many flair players on the pitch as possible and feed them and let them cause havoc. So buckle in, and hopefully we give the fans something to sing about."

Tamworth have won just one of their opening seven games, and are 22nd in the table, conceding 19 goals so far.

"They're very good at what they do. They play two up. They try to bring chaos to a game, and they want it to be transitional" Dyer added.

"That's why they've scored a lot of goals (13), but I think it's also why they've conceded a lot of goals, too (19). We feel we can really expose their weaknesses.

"We'll make a few changes and try to get some real freshness. They pose a threat, but if we do what we want to do I think this game should be ok for us."

articles.title: Kentucky Wildcats crack top ten for elite Class of 2027 forward
articles.summary: AJ Williams is down to ten schools, and the Kentucky Wildcats, among with many other top programs, are among those listed.
articles.body:
AJ Williams is down to ten, and Mark Pope's Kentucky Wildcats are among those listed.

Pope hasn't had the best luck recruiting since making the jump to Kentucky, but things are starting to change. The addition of Class of 2027 forward Ryan Hampton marked a huge win for Pope and his staff, and there have been plenty of other elite recruits that are still including Kentucky as they start to narrow their options down.

Williams was one of the latest to drop an updated list of where he's going to play next season, and listed as the top player from Georgia and the second-best small forward, every program in the nation would love to attract the 6-foot-7 star. Here's the list: BYU, Georgia, Mississippi State, Illinois, Duke, Auburn, Kentucky, North Carolina, Arkansas, and Georgia Tech. It's an interesting list, one that doesn't include other blue-blood programs like Michigan State or Kansas.

Williams is going to finish up his high school career at Eagle's Landing Christian Academy. He's been ranked as the fifth-best player in the nation, per 247Sports, and was the top player in the Class of 2028 before reclassifying. There's good reason to believe that the 17-year-old forward could be the best player in the class as well. He dominated the Nike EYBL 17U circuit.

"Williams, 17, played on the Nike EYBL 17U circuit this summer with Team CP3 and established himself as one of the league's most productive scorers. He averaged 20.9 points, 8.1 rebounds and 1.4 assists while shooting 41.8 percent from the field and 31.1 percent from 3-point range," Tobias Bass and Brendan Marks of the New York Times wrote.

The excitement around the star forward is real, and hopefully he'll be able to bring that to Kentucky next season.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest fans' plea over stadium expansion
articles.summary: A fan group says the proposed City Ground development is a "historic opportunity for our region".
articles.body:
A Nottingham Forest supporters' group has written an open letter asking councillors to back expansion plans for its stadium, saying "it is the City Ground's time".

Rushcliffe Borough Council's planning committee will meet on Wednesday to consider applications from the club on proposed changes to the ground.

In June last year, the committee granted full planning permission to increase its overall capacity to 35,000, followed in January by the club submitting another set of applications to take the capacity to more than 50,000.

The Nottingham Forest Supporters' Trust (NFST) urged the authority not to let concerns over transport and supporter movement on matchdays further delay the project.

The applications consist of a bid for full planning permission to redevelop the Peter Taylor Stand and Trent End, as well as for "demolition of existing buildings/structures", and outline planning permission to redevelop the Brian Clough Stand.

Rushcliffe's planning officers have recommended councillors on the committee approve the applications, subject to conditions.

It comes days after MPs in Nottingham issued a joint statement backing development of the stadium.

The trust's letter to the committee calls Wednesday's vote a "historic opportunity for our region", adding the message was "clear and overwhelming" from fans in their support of the proposals.

Asif Naidu, NFST chair, said: "Wednesday is a historic opportunity to secure the future of our historic home. We simply have to grasp it.

"The case for approval is incredibly strong. It has clear and widespread support across the region, the club has outgrown the current ground and it is a golden and rare investment opportunity.

"Any concerns over transport and supporter flow, while understandable, can be resolved and are manageable, so they shouldn't be a barrier to giving the project the go-ahead.

"It is the City Ground's time. Let's make history on Wednesday."

articles.title: McBurnie & seven uncapped names in Scotland squad
articles.summary: Hull City forward Oli McBurnie is called up to the Scotland squad for the first time in five years while seven uncapped make new head coach Sebastien Pocogno...
articles.body:
Oli McBurnie has been called up to the Scotland squad for the first time in five years, with new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli saying the Hull City forward fits his "style of play".

Uncapped Luis Binks , Colby Donovan, Jon McCracken , Josh McPake and Stephen Welsh also makes Pocognoli's first selection. As expected, Stoke defender Luke Graham and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure receive their first senior call-ups.

Scott Bain , Kieron Bowie , Josh Doig , Lennon Miller and James Wilson are recalled but Che Adams misses out. Napoli midfielder Billy Gilmour , 25, returns after missing the World Cup injured.

McBurnie, 30, first featured for his country in 2018 and won the last of his 16 caps in 2021.

He has never scored for Scotland but did net one of the penalties in the shootout that sealed a place at the delayed Euro 2020 finals.

"It's a new opportunity for some players, a really new beginning for the other ones," said Pocognoli.

"I have to start a new journey, start a new book. The most important is regarding the style of play that I want to produce on the pitch. We need to adapt quick.

"To be honest, I can extend this list because I have to make some choices. There are a lot of names who can be also in that squad for that camp. Players who are not there is because for the style of play, it can be from injury or playing time.

"There's many players that I would like to call up. The door is never closed."

Binks, 25, has previously played age grade football for England and Scotland and Pocognoli said in reference to the Brondby player: "The timing was right with him."

Right-back Donovan, 20, has come to prominence filling in for injured Canada right-back Alistair Johnston in Celtic's side this season. Like McBurnie, he has been capped at under-19 and under-21 level. Pocognoli said Donovan had "played some good games" and had dealt with "expectation".

Graham was part of Scotland's pre-World Cup training camp in May after a breakthrough campaign with Dundee, winning the Scottish Premiership club's players' player and young player of the year awards.

The 22-year-old was an unused substitute in the country's send-off friendly win against Curacao , which was also Steve Clarke's last game in the dugout at Hampden Park.

The defender, who has three caps at under-21 level, has started strongly for The Potters in the Championship, who are unbeaten in their past four games, with Graham an ever-present.

Four-time capped Falkirk goalkeeper Bain, 34, and Bradford City keeper Jon McCracken, 26, were in squads named by Pocognoli's predecessor Clarke. Bain and McCracken join Angus Gunn and Liam Kelly in the goalkeeping pool.

And Pocognoli commented: "I will not talk about my number one and number two today.

"We have a strong generation in the past. Now we need just to rebirth this but we have good quality. We have experienced goalkeepers and we have some young talents."

Pocognoli's compatriot, Heart of Midlothian head coach Wouter Vrancken, was "confident" there would be a few players from the Tynecastle club included and winger McPake, 25, and 19-year-old attacking club-mate James Wilson, who has two caps, are recognised for their early-season performances. However, Hearts winger Calvin Miller misses out.

Swansea City defender Stephen Welsh, 26, may win his first cap while Sassuolo forward Bowie, 23, and left-back Doig, 24, as well as Udinese midfielder Miller, 20, make the cut.

Former Rangers academy product Ure was in demand across Europe after a free-scoring spell - 20 goals and three assists in 20 matches - that took Sirius to the top of the table in Sweden and it resulted in a £5.5m summer transfer to La Liga with Sevilla.

Ure, 22, has yet to find the target in Spain , but given his eligibility for Ukraine, the new head coach appears tempted to tie him down as soon as possible.

"Players who are there are performing well," said Pocognoli. "Robbie is now challenging to adjust to La Liga level."

The inclusion of Bowie, McBurnie, Ure and Wilson come as reports indicate Torino 's Adams is injured while Rangers forward Lawrence Shankland is out for up to four months with a hamstring injury.

Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay , 29, is unavailable, having recently had minor heart surgery.

Of the 28 named in this squad, 14 were part of this summer's World Cup.

Gunn and Kelly, defenders Jack Hendry , Aaron Hickey , Scott McKenna , Nathan Patterson , Andy Robertson and Kieran Tierney , midfielders Ryan Christie , Lewis Ferguson , John McGinn and Kenny McLean and forwards Findlay Curtis and Ben Gannon-Doak are all retained.

Goalkeeper Craig Gordon has retired while Grant Hanley has recently returned to fitness at Hibernian while Rangers defender John Souttar has not played this season amid reports linking him with Aris Thessaloniki.

Defenders Dominic Hyam and Anthony Ralston , midfielder Tyler Fletcher and forwards Lyndon Dykes , George Hirst and Ross Stewart miss out.

When asked about the possibility of calling up Scotland-qualified Newcastle winger Harvey Barnes , 28, and Everton midfielder Hayden Hackney , 24, Pocognoli said he was "aware of everything and about the feeling of everybody" and said "it's about timing."

"I don't want to convince players," he explained. "They need to be open to representing in the natural way, the country. We'll see in the future."

Since Pocognoli was announced as Clarke's successor - the former Kilmarnock manager having resigned after the Scots failed to qualify for the knockout stages of a major tournament for the first time - the expectation was that the Belgian would look to freshen up an ageing squad.

Pocognoli will take charge of Scotland for the first time on Saturday, 26 September in the Scots' Nations League B opener against Slovenia and his debut in the Hampden dugout will be three days later against Switzerland .

A trip to face North Macedonia on 3 October follows before a home tie with Slovenia three days afterwards.

And the Belgian said: "We have a good mix between experienced players, new faces, first cap players, young lads, players who are back.

"We have a lot of leaders, we have a lot of players who know how to win games.

"We want to be ambitious in this Nations League. We have to use this Nations League to try things, to experiment things but the most important is to be ambitious."

articles.title: El reto de Ander Martín y Esther Briz en el Europeo de Beach Sprint: subir al podio donde empezó todo
articles.standfirst: La Línea de la Concepción acoge hasta el domingo el campeonato continental y de remo de mar. Allí remaron juntos por primera vez hace cinco años. Esta vez lo harán por separado
articles.summary: La Línea de la Concepción acoge hasta el domingo el campeonato continental y de remo de mar. Allí remaron juntos por primera vez hace cinco años. Esta vez lo harán por separado
articles.body: “La primera vez que salí corriendo por una playa para meterme al barco fue con Ander en La Línea, en el selectivo que se hizo aquí hace cinco años. Al final ganamos y clasificamos el barco para el Mundial”, rememora Esther Briz, olímpica junto a Aina Cid en París 2024 en dos sin timonel y ganadora este año de la regata Oxford-Cambridge. Nunca antes había probado el Beach Sprint, modalidad olímpica que se estrena en Los Ángeles 2028, pero su amigo Ander Martín la convenció para competir juntos. La maña estaba un poco agobiada la noche anterior a su estreno. “Esther no sabía cómo subir al barco”, desvela entre risas el alicantino, que pese a todo estaba convencido de que iba a ir bien. Son amigos desde alevines y siempre ha habido mucha química entre ellos. En el mar no fue una excepción. Regresan a La Línea de la Concepción (Cádiz), que acoge los Europeos de Beach Sprint y larga distancia hasta el domingo, convertidos en dos bazas de medalla. Aunque esta vez no competirán juntos. Pese a que ganaron los selectivos de este año tanto en individual como en mixto, la decisión técnica de la Federación Española de Remo es que nadie doble, por lo que Martín, que el año pasado fue plata continental, y Briz han elegido competir de forma individual. “En el doble te la juegas todo a una carta y en individual hay dos opciones. Pero seguimos entrenando en doble”, aclaran. Porque el objetivo es el podio en Los Ángeles 2028. Por eso, a lo largo de estos meses Ander ha viajado a Oxford, donde Esther estudiaba un MBA, y ella ha estado yendo y viniendo al CAR de Murcia y al RCN de Torrevieja, donde tienen su base hasta los Juegos. Desde principios de julio ambos se han instalado allí, aunque la zaragozana ha ido casi a diario al módulo de hipoxia del CAR de Los Alcázares para llegar al Europeo lo mejor posible. Ander ya lo hizo mientras ella estaba en Inglaterra. Esther, que afronta la cita tras su oro en el Pharoes Trophy, se ha perdido su graduación por la competición. “Si gano medalla me llevaré el birrete y la capa para celebrarlo”, dice riendo. “He tenido un año muy duro, casi sin descanso, pero vengo con confianza. Estoy bien física y mentalmente”, dice. Ander también tiene muy buenas sensaciones. “Nunca he competido en La Línea sin haberme llevado medalla, nacional o internacional. Mi objetivo en el Europeo es disfrutar. Siempre salgo a por el oro, pero si disfruto irá bien. Y no me importa la presión, cuanta más hay mejor funciono”, asegura. Rodeados del mejor equipo -técnico en remo y atletismo, fisiológico, biomecánico, médico, nutricionista- han ido mejorando estos meses en todos los aspecto. Uno de ello, la parte de la carrera en la playa antes de subirse a la embarcación. Han estado haciendo entrenamientos específicos. "Esther corre muy bien, tiene más mérito hacerme correr bien a mí. Me cuesta mucho. Si son 30 metros es lo mío, ya más...", confiesa Martín. También han trabajado la parte mental. "Por mucho que entrenes, lo que marca la diferencia es la cabeza. El factor concentración es clave. Es más de un 60%. En mi caso me cuesta mucho porque desde pequeño tengo déficit de atención e hiperactividad. Este año he buscado ayuda para desarrollar herramientas y confío en hacerlo con la menor ayuda posible", explica a MARCA. Esther lleva tiempo trabajando con una psicóloga. "Para mí es importante para estar mentalmente al cien por cien. Yo voy siempre a tope con mil cosas y me ayuda a estar tranquila y relajada", explica. En La Línea empezó todo hace cinco años. En La Línea se disputó también el selectivo que les abrió la puerta a este Europeo. Y en La Línea quieren dar ahora otro paso hacia Los Ángeles. El sueño olímpico todavía queda lejos, pero el camino ya está trazado. En ese camino estarán acompañados por el RCN de Torrevieja y el Ayuntamiento de esta localidad alicantina, el Proyecto FER, Quirón Salud y Grupo Enhol y Rilastil, compañeros de viaje para que puedan brillar en LA2028. Cinco años después de aquella primera carrera por la arena, vuelven al lugar donde empezó todo. Y esta vez saben exactamente hacia dónde quieren remar.

articles.title: B/R NHL Staff Predictions For All 2027 NHL Playoff Teams
articles.summary: The long road to the 2027 Stanley Cup begins this week as all 32 teams report for training camp.
articles.body:
The long road to the 2027 Stanley Cup begins this week as all 32 teams report for training camp.

The bulls-eye will be on the defending champion Hurricanes, but before we get to the Cup, we have to determine which teams will make the postseason.

Our B/R NHL Staff provided their picks for all 16 teams that will make the 2027 NHL Playoffs.

Disagree with our panel? Submit your thoughts now in the comments section of the app!

Rising Young Teams Could Challenge Veteran Clubs

A changing of the guard that began last season carries on in 2026-27.

Rising young teams, like the Canadiens, Flyers and Sabres in the Eastern Conference, and the Sharks and Ducks in the Western Conference, will challenge long-established veterans teams for dominance in the standings.

Those teams are still works in progress, but some (like the Canadiens, Sabres, and Sharks) have progressed better and faster than anticipated.

Several of those veteran teams, like the Lightning, Hurricanes, Stars, Avalanche, and Wild, possess enough talent in their prime to remain playoff teams and potential Stanley Cup contenders. For some, however, this could be their last good season before the inevitable decline begins.

Following a summer of significant player movement, the Capitals have a roster that (on paper) could make them among the league's best. Still, they are a team in transition, with this season expected to be Alex Ovechkin's last.

The Panthers and Oilers land among the wild card amid concerns about their goaltending and other roster issues. The Bruins are still retooling while the Mammoth are a promising team in a tough division.

As esteemed colleague Lyle R. mentioned, we saw younger teams take some huge steps last season. Macklin Celebrini's breakout fueled the ahead-of-schedule Sharks as they dipped their fin into the playoff race, and the Canadiens gave us some of the most exciting games of the entire playoffs on their run to the ECF.

This season, the young teams will keep rising: The Sharks and the additions they've made will make it to the playoffs, the Canadiens will get sturdier, the Sabres will hang in there despite big changes, and the Ducks will make the most of Leo Carlsson's payday.

The big challenges out East? The Panthers are back, baby. They're healthy as ever; they've got two Tkachuk brothers in the fold, and they're hungry to reach dynasty status. The Capitals narrowly missed the playoffs last season with a record that would've punched a ticket in the West. Now, Alex Ovechkin is back, with the help of Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou, to end a legendary career on a high note.

Out West, the Oilers have made some drastic moves in response to growing pressure and the final year of Connor McDavid's contract. It's hard to say if the drama will help or hurt the team's Cup hopes until the puck drops on the season, but I'm not going to bet against the best player in the world in the most desperate state we've seen him in.

Still, as we saw last season, the Oilers have begun to lose the footrace against speedier, younger teams in their division. While I'm confident they will make the playoffs, I have a hard time believing they'll beat out that kind of up-and-comer talent and attitude with miserable brute force.

Do you like postseason turnover in your predictions? Fitz is your guy.

My calculations have no fewer than six teams in the 2026-27 tournament who were not in the 2025-26 mix, including youthful gate-crashers like New Jersey in the East and San Jose out West, while the others are familiar playoff commodities like Florida (remember them?), Washington, Toronto and Winnipeg.

That means it'll be a long season in Pennsylvania, where both Philadelphia and Pittsburgh are churned out of the Eastern race, Ottawa feels the Brady Tkachuk loss especially as the new Panthers advance, and a new regime in Toronto sneaks in while second-year man Marco Sturm and Boston take a seat.

Out West, it's time to give Macklin Celebrini and the Sharks their flowers, but it'll mean last year's darlings from Anaheim fall out of the mix along with the crosstown Los Angeles Kings. And that leaves room for the Winnipeg Jets, too, as muscle memory gets them closer to their Presidents' Trophy level of 2024-25.

It says here that Florida makes it all the way back from last season's injury-sopped oblivion. And who better for them to face in the final round than Connor McDavid and the Oilers, though we concede there's just as real a chance they're looking for a coach by American Thanksgiving and shopping No. 97 at the trade deadline.

Trades That Could Happen Before Training Camp

Expect a Revival in the Metropolitan Division

I'm seeing a Metropolitan Division revival. The Hurricanes' stature speaks for itself. The New Jersey Devils, under new leadership, look to return to the run-and-gun hockey that served them well in the past, while adding some heavy play drivers such as Luke Evangelista. I nearly ranked them first in the division.

Meanwhile, the Rangers still have many problems, but GM Chris Drury has raised the floor. The top-four on defense is about as good as any in the NHL. JT Miller will presumably be healthy. The bottom six has the potential to be at least average. To me, they're a playoff team.

The Atlantic will be a gauntlet, and you can credibly rank the top-three teams in any order. The Panthers' forward group may be the best in the NHL, but I do wonder if defense and goaltending leave them slipping just behind Tampa Bay and Buffalo.

The West feels predictable, though I struggled to find a credible suitor for the second wild-card spot. I'll take a flyer on the Blues. There should be more stability this season, and strong campaigns from up-and-comers like Jimmy Snuggerud and Dalibor Dvorsky could allow for a run. Perhaps notably, the San Jose Sharks are missing. Macklin Celebrini alone may carry them into the playoffs, but I am not at all buying the defensive moves made this summer.

It would be so easy to pick last year's playoff field, run it back with the same 16 teams, and decide that things will be different in some ways. But there's no way that happens... right? No shot.

The Capitals improved immensely, adding Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou, as did the Panthers with Brady Tkachuk and the return of Aleksander Barkov. The Oilers radically changed their on-ice leadership with Mike Babcock. The Canadiens made themselves more difficult to deal with by adding Chris Kreider.

There might still be more moves to come that change the outlook of the league, but where things get volatile in the East is how interchangeable the Metropolitan Division is and how ruthless the Atlantic is. The defending champion Hurricanes seem like locks, but the rest of the Metro will be wild. Sure, the Caps will bounce back, but everyone else will play ro-sham-bo, and the Islanders, with Ilya Sorokin in goal, Matthew Schaefer a year older, and Peter DeBoer in charge, seem like the kind of group that can win in a street fight among the rest of the division.

The Atlantic will be incredible. There's heat and hate all over the division, as the Lightning demonstrated by how they treated just about everyone who looked at them funny. The Canadiens, Sabres, and Panthers will join them in a battle royale atop the division, with the Bruins, Senators, and Maple Leafs fighting for the other wild card, with teams from the Metropolitan Division

In the West, it's hard to see how things change drastically in the Central. Colorado, Minnesota, and Dallas are among the best teams in the league, and with Utah trying to join the party, that makes things a bit more interesting. St. Louis or Nashville might creep in, and if things break really right, maybe Chicago or Winnipeg, but this division is so stacked on top it's hard to see things change.

In the Pacific, though, this really feels strange. Vegas' talent is hard to ignore, and the Sharks are on the rise. Even though the Ducks had a rough summer, they're still very good, and the Oilers still have Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl. The Kings are in that mix too, but how they adjust without Anže Kopitar will be interesting.

articles.title: Connor Bedard Named 37th Captain in Blackhawks History Ahead of 2026-27 NHL Season
articles.summary: Connor Bedard will head into his fourth NHL season wearing the 'C' for the Chicago Blackhawks.
articles.body:
Connor Bedard will head into his fourth NHL season wearing the 'C' for the Chicago Blackhawks.

The Blackhawks named Bedard the 37th captain in franchise history ahead of the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

Staff Predictions for Every Playoff Team 🔮

The news comes after the Blackhawks signed Bedard to a five-year, $15 million AAV deal that will keep him under contract through the 2030-31 campaign.

The forward is expected to start the campaign on injured reserve after undergoing shoulder surgery this offseason.

Bedard is the third player to lead the Blackhawks since 2008, when Jonathan Toews took over the captaincy.

Toews helped lead the Blackhawks to three Stanley Cups between 2010 and 2015 before leaving the team following the 2022-23 season.

The role was most recently filled by Nick Foligno, who has served as captain for the last two seasons.

Bedard wore a letter for the first time in the 2025-26 campaign as an alternate to Foligno, who was traded to the Minnesota Wild in March.

The captaincy marks the next step in the Blackhawks rebuilding their team around Bedard, a move that has been in progress since the franchise selected him at the top of the 2023 draft.

Bedard started off his NHL career by winning the Calder Trophy despite breaking his jaw midway through his rookie 2023-24 campaign.

He took a step forward in his third season by recording career highs in goals (30), assists (45) and points (75) despite missing 12 games with a right shoulder injury.

Bedard is set to miss more time to start out the 2026-27 campaign after suffering another shoulder injury while practicing in July. The Blackhawks have indicated he is expected to return in November.

The Hawks haven't gotten any closer to the playoffs in Bedard's first three seasons, each of which the team has finished at the bottom of the Central Division.

After acquiring and extending defenseman Bowen Byram and reuniting with veteran winger Patrick Kane this offseason, the Blackhawks will be hoping Bedard can start off his captaincy by helping his team contend for its first postseason run since 2020.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s chess contingent has finally secured hotel accommodation in Samarkand after an unexpected crisis delayed room allotments on the eve of the 46th Chess Olympiad.The Indian team arrived in Uzbekistan on Tuesday, but several players were left waiting at their hotel for hours after learning that their reservations had not been properly communicated to the property by the local organising committee (LOC).The team was scheduled to stay at the Silk Road by Minyoun hotel. Men’s team captain Srinath Narayanan took to social media to express his frustration, saying the contingent had landed nearly five hours earlier but still had no clarity on when rooms would be allotted.The All India Chess Federation (AICF) president Nitin Narang intervened in the situation and asked FIDE to arrange accommodation for the players.Throughout the day, Narang remained in discussions with FIDE and the organising committee to resolve the issue.“We took up the matter very strongly with both the LOC and FIDE. "But I am relieved that the players have now been accommodated and are finally in their rooms."The Indian contingent had 16 rooms reserved for them, 14 of which have so far been confirmed. articles.title: Ryan Leonard, Capitals Agree to $84 Million Contract, Full Details Ahead of 2026 NHL Season
articles.summary: The Washington Capitals are locking in Ryan Leonard for the long term after his 20-goal rookie season.
articles.body:
The Washington Capitals are locking in Ryan Leonard for the long term after his 20-goal rookie season.

Leonard and the Capitals have agreed to an eight-year, $10.5 million AAV extension ahead of the 2026-27 season, the franchise announced Tuesday.

Leonard, 21, was previously set to hit restricted free agency after playing out the last season of his rookie deal in 2026-27.

The extension will keep Leonard, who posted 45 points (20 goals, 25 assists) in 75 games last season, under contract through his age-29 season in 2034-35.

Leonard spent most of last season skating in the Capitals' bottom six alongside Connor McMichael and Justin Sourdif.

That arrangement will change this fall given that McMichael has since been traded to and re-signed by the St. Louis Blues.

Leonard will also return to his role on a Capitals power play looking to bounce back after ranking 25th in the NHL with a 17.8 percent success rate last season.

The Capitals initially selected Leonard with the eighth pick of the 2023 draft. He starred in two seasons with Boston College before making his NHL debut late in a 2024-25 campaign that ended with the Caps making it to the second round.

Leonard made the jump to a full-time roster spot last season, during which his importance to the Capitals became obvious when he was placed on injured serve with an upper-body injury in December.

Capitals president of hockey operations Brian MacLellan later pointed to that stretch, over which the Capitals went 2-3-2, as an inflection point in a season that ended without a playoff run.

Leonard will now help the Capitals push for a postseason return in what might be Alex Ovechkin's final NHL season, as well as a play a key role in the franchise's future past Ovechkin's eventual retirement.

Now the longest-tenured player in Washington, D.C., Leonard joins a long-term Capitals core already featuring Tom Wilson, Jordan Kyrou, Pierre-Luc Dubois, Alex Tuch, Jakob Chychrun, Martin Fehervary and Logan Thompson, all of whom are signed through the 2030-31 campaign.

articles.title: Lil Yachty Says He Feels 'Like S--t' After WWE Debut Match, 'Most Pain I Ever Felt in My Life'
articles.summary: After making his WWE in-ring debut at Sunday Night's Main Event on Sept. 6, rapper Lil Yachty discussed the toll it took on him physically.
articles.body:
After making his WWE in-ring debut at Sunday Night's Main Event on Sept. 6, rapper Lil Yachty discussed the toll it took on him physically.

During an appearance on Insight with Chris Van Vliet (beginning at the 1:28 mark) the day after his debut match against Baron Corbin, Yachty said he felt "like s--t," before adding, "I feel like someone hit me with a bag of bricks."

Buzz: Zayn's Title Win Opposed Backstage 👀

After managing Trick Williams in recent months, Yachty finally had an official match at Sunday Night's Main Event, and the stakes were high.

If Yachty could last five minutes with Corbin without getting pinned or submitted, Trick would receive another shot at the U.S. title.

Yachty somehow managed to make it to the five-minute mark despite absorbing a ton of punishment, which led to Williams beating Corbin to become a two-time United States champion.

In speaking to Van Vliet (h/t Fightful Select ), Yachty further explained the pain he was feeling after SNME, saying, "When I woke up this morning, my shoulder felt dislocated. My kneecaps, my shins. I couldn't even tighten my hand. As the day goes on, everything's loosening up. When I first sat up in bed, it was the most pain I ever felt in my life. Shins, knees, whatever this is behind the kneecap, my back, my lower back. I feel like I'm wrestling for 20 years. Man, it's bad."

A longtime pro wrestling fan, Yachty has often been seen seated front row at WWE events over the years, but he became an actual part of the show in March when he began accompanying Trick to the ring.

Despite his lack of experience in the wrestling business, it didn't take long before Yachty started getting physically involved, as he was on the receiving end of punishment from Sami Zayn leading up to and coming out of WrestleMania 42.

When Corbin beat Williams for the United States Championship at SummerSlam, it came after Corbin put Yachty through a table in what was the biggest spot of his young career to that point.

Now, Yachty has his first match under his belt and has managed to persevere through the pain, which suggests there could be even more in his future.

articles.title: La familia de Kalie McCrystal se despide de ella tras no ser encontrada en el Cervino
articles.standfirst: Su madre y hermana hablan de una caída como la causa que provocó su desaparición el 1 de septiembre en esta montaña de los Alpes
articles.summary: Su madre y hermana hablan de una caída como la causa que provocó su desaparición el 1 de septiembre en esta montaña de los Alpes
articles.body: La familia de Kalie McCrystal, la corredora de montaña canadiense que desapareció mientras entrenaba en el Matterhorn (montaña de 4.478 m, también conocido con el nombre de Cervino) ha emitido un comunicado en el que se despide de ella. Su madre, Wendy Cooper, y su hermana, Jody McCrystal, asumen que no se ha podido encontrar su cuerpo: "A pesar de los esfuerzos de tantas personas durante las últimas semanas, la búsqueda no nos ha llevado a Kalie. Este no es el resultado que ninguno de nosotros esperaba, y es muy difícil de aceptar". McCrystal había viajado a esta zona de los Alpes para intentar ascender y descender el Cervino por la ruta de la Cresta del León, en la vertiente italiana, en menos de cinco horas y batir el récord mundial de velocidad de ascenso y descenso de esta cima. La última vez que se confirmó que se había visto a McCrystal fue la tarde del 1 de septiembre, cuando un grupo de escaladores polacos la avistó mientras descendían la montaña cerca del Pic Tyndall. "Desde entonces, los rescatistas de montaña han intentado incansablemente seguir todas las pistas posibles. Para nosotros, como familia, ha significado muchísimo saber que se estaba haciendo todo lo humanamente posible durante toda la búsqueda. Les estaremos eternamente agradecidos por ello", escriben la madre y hermana de Kalie McCrystal. El comunicado apunta también a la causa que provocó al pérdida de contacto con McCrystal": "A pesar de las excepcionales habilidades y experiencia de Kalie en montañismo técnico, incluyendo sus experiencias previas en el propio Matterhorn, todo lo que sabemos ahora indica que cayó durante el descenso". "Su pérdida dejará un enorme vacío en la comunidad de corredores de montaña, en Squamish —su ciudad natal— y más allá. Nada volverá a ser igual para nuestra familia. Kalie significaba muchísimo para nosotros como hermana e hija, y su pérdida es algo que llevaremos con nosotros para siempre", prosigue el comunicado. "Aunque deseábamos con todas nuestras fuerzas haberla encontrado, nos reconforta saber que hasta sus últimos momentos hizo lo que la hacía sentir más viva, y que ahora permanece en las montañas donde se sentía más en casa", concluyen Wendy Cooper, y su hermana, Jody McCrystal.

articles.title: Donovan Mitchell’s Cavs Arrival Has A Wild 15-Year Twist
articles.summary: Donovan Mitchell has become one of the most important players in Cleveland, but the path that brought him there is far more complicated than one blockbuster...
articles.body:
Donovan Mitchell has become one of the most important players in Cleveland , but the path that brought him there is far more complicated than one blockbuster trade. The Cavaliers spent years making moves that produced value at different points, and one of those decisions is tied to a part of the franchise's history that seems completely unrelated to Mitchell.

That connection stretches across multiple eras of Cleveland basketball. Players came and went, draft picks changed hands, and the Cavaliers kept turning one asset into another while building toward a much bigger payoff.

Donovan Mitchell 's Cleveland Story Has An Unexpected Link

The first major piece of the chain came in 2011, when Cleveland sent Mo Williams and Jamario Moon to the Los Angeles Clippers . In return, the Cavaliers received Baron Davis and an unprotected first-round pick.

That pick quickly became much more valuable than anyone could have expected. Cleveland landed the No. 1 selection in the 2011 NBA Draft and used it to take Kyrie Irving , giving the franchise a future All-Star who would eventually become one of the biggest names in Cavaliers history.

Irving later became part of another important transaction when Cleveland sent him to the Boston Celtics in 2017. The Cavaliers received several assets in that deal, including a first-round pick that originally belonged to the Brooklyn Nets .

Cleveland eventually used that selection to draft Collin Sexton with the No. 8 pick in 2018. At that point, the connection to Mitchell still seemed almost impossible to see.

The Cavaliers Finally Cash In On The Old Assets

Sexton became the next link in the chain. After four seasons in Cleveland, he was included in the package the Cavaliers sent to the Utah Jazz for Mitchell in 2022.

The deal brought Mitchell to Cleveland in exchange for Sexton, Lauri Markkanen , Ochai Agbaji , three first-round picks and two pick swaps. What looked like a completely new chapter for the Cavaliers was actually connected to years of earlier asset management.

That is what makes Mitchell's arrival so unusual. One of the players used to acquire him was acquired via a draft pick that came through another trade, which in turn stemmed from an earlier decision to move Williams and Moon.

The Cavaliers did not know in 2011 that they were setting up a future path to Donovan Mitchell. They simply made a trade, then kept making decisions with the assets that followed.

Fifteen years later, that chain had helped Cleveland build a team around another All-Star guard. The move that started with Mo Williams and Jamario Moon ultimately became part of the long road that led the Cavaliers to Mitchell.

articles.title: Rangers have 'more gears to go' as Penrice eyes derby double
articles.summary: James Penrice has urged resurgent Rangers to follow up their "brilliant" League Cup win over Celtic by beating the Premiership leaders at Parkhead this weeke...
articles.body:
James Penrice has urged resurgent Rangers to follow up their "brilliant" League Cup win over Celtic by beating the Premiership leaders at Parkhead this weekend.

The left-back, on loan from AEK Athens, shone in a midfield role in his Old Firm debut as Rangers swept aside their arch rivals 3-0 at Ibrox last Sunday to reach the semi-finals.

He acknowledges the second derby of the season will be a "very different game" but insists Rangers head to Celtic Park intent on victory.

Speaking at an event to launch Rangers Charity Foundation's partnership with Down's Syndrome Scotland, the 27-year-old reflected on a "memorable Sunday".

He said: "You've seen a real team performance and I think from the get-go we were brilliant. We need to park Sunday and focus on the league now so it needs to be followed up this Sunday.

"I definitely think we've got more gears to go but there's evidence that it's a lot better. But let's not get too far in front of ourselves, Sunday's massive and ultimately we need to go there and win the game, so we'll be looking to do that."

After a challenging start to the season, including failing to qualify for European competition, Rangers now won five matches in a row - clear evidence things are coming together, according to Penrice.

"I feel like over the last couple of weeks we've been winning games in that sort of way where it's everyone together, but it just made it 100 times better that it was a full stadium," he added.

"You've seen after the game, everyone was in it together and it can only give us confidence going into the next run of games where we need to keep winning.

"Definitely it feels like a real team and that's probably the biggest compliment I can give the boys and for the manager as well. From a difficult position, we've managed to turn it, but it's not fully turned yet, we've still got a lot of work to do."

Penrice says playing in an Old Firm match was always on his "footballing bucket list" and the first instalment surpassed his expectations.

"The noise just when we came on the pitch and during the warm-up was wild," he said.

"But you have to perform and it makes it all the better that we managed to walk away with the win. It was a very memorable Sunday."

With no Rangers fans at Celtic Park in the Premiership match this Sunday, Penrice acknowledges the atmosphere will be somewhat less welcoming.

"From our players' point of view, we don't go there and worry about fans. We think the game will be different," he said.

"They'll probably change stuff, we'll probably change stuff. It'll be a different game but we'll go there with the mindset that we're going to win. That's what you need to do as a Rangers player, you need to go to these places and win."

articles.title: Brian Angelichio Saw Something He Liked From Steelers’ Deep Passing Game Despite Missed Chances
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers got the result they wanted in Week 1; however, their passing game still left plenty on the table. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers looked mu...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers got the result they wanted in Week 1; however, their passing game still left plenty on the table. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers looked much more willing to push the ball downfield than he did last season, and the Steelers found ways to test the Atlanta Falcons' coverage early.

There were missed chances along the way. Some throws didn't even connect, and the offense never found a perfect rhythm. Still, offensive coordinator Brian Angelichio came away encouraged by one part of the attack.

Brian Angelichio Sees Progress In Pittsburgh Steelers ' Downfield Passing Game

On September 15, t he Steelers OC Angelichio explained why he liked what he saw from the team's deep passing approach in the 20-13 win over the Falcons. The Steelers entered the game wanting to take shots and make the Falcons defend the entire field.

"I certainly think comfort has a lot to do with it, but that was something that we wanted to do was take some shots and try to stress the coverage. Unfortunately, we had some ops at some and we didn't quite execute the way we wanted to."

And the results were noticeable too. The veteran QB held the ball longer and pushed his throws farther downfield than he did during his first season in Pittsburgh . According to NFL Next Gen Stats, his average time to throw was 2.95 seconds, while his intended air yards sat at 9.5.

That was a pretty big change from 2025. Rodgers had the quickest average time to throw among starting quarterbacks last season at 2.59 seconds, while his 6.0 average intended air yards ranked as the shortest among starters.

In this case, it was evident that the Steelers wanted to create something big. The Steelers also faced many single-high coverages from the Falcons, giving the 42-year-old the opportunity to create something vertical. Michael Pittman Jr. took full advantage of his three targets, while other opportunities in the air remained unconverted.

One of the most notable opportunities lost was that of Roman Wilson . He earned himself a pass interference call for a 37-yard play that would've resulted in a touchdown without it. Then Wilson got another opportunity in the end zone, although he failed to complete the play while trying to fall down.

That is where the Steelers' opener gets interesting. The deep shots were there; however, the execution was not always clean . Head coach Mike McCarthy admitted Monday that the offense felt "herky jerky" at times and said he did not like the lack of consistent rhythm. Still, he liked the mentality behind the attack and pointed to the middle of the field as a major part of what Pittsburgh wants to build around.

The Steelers now have a full game of tape to work from before facing the New England Patriots in Week 2. The Falcons showed them what worked, what missed, and where Rodgers can keep attacking. For Angelichio, the missed throws did not erase the bigger takeaway: the Steelers wanted to stretch coverage, and it finally showed that intent.

articles.title: Fabrizio Romano: Man United have made Michael Carrick decision after poor start
articles.summary: Michael Carrick Backed by Manchester United Despite Slow Start as Left-Back Gap RemainsManchester United have no immediate plans to change manager, despite a...
articles.body:
Michael Carrick Backed by Manchester United Despite Slow Start as Left-Back Gap Remains

Manchester United have no immediate plans to change manager, despite a frustrating opening to the Premier League campaign that has left Michael Carrick under early scrutiny. Four points from four matches is an underwhelming return by any standard, and the 1-0 home defeat to Manchester City , against 10 men for part of the contest, has naturally sharpened focus around Old Trafford.

Yet the message coming from inside the club is calm rather than reactive. As reported by Fabrizio Romano on his YouTube channel, United's hierarchy remain aligned behind Carrick and still believe he is the right man to lead the project forward. That backing appears significant given the wider context, with Carrick having secured the role permanently after steering the club to third place and Champions League qualification during his interim spell last season.

Manchester United hierarchy staying patient

The clearest indication from this update is that Manchester United are trying to avoid short-term thinking. "Man Utd absolutely remain convinced that the future will be bright under Michael Carrick," Romano said on his YouTube channel. That stance has not changed even after a poor run of early results, with senior figures viewing the current position as disappointing but not yet alarming.

There is also recognition internally that the squad did not emerge from the summer exactly as planned. United wanted to recruit at left-back, and Lewis Hall was admired, but the club ultimately stepped away when the preferred deal could not be completed. The feeling was that there was little value in making a signing for the sake of appearances, particularly in a position where quality and suitability were prioritised over speed.

Left-back issue still part of the wider picture

That missing addition matters. Balance in wide areas remains important to how Carrick wants his side to build attacks and control transitions, and a specialist left-back may have eased some of the current structural issues. It does not explain everything about the slow start, but it forms part of the backdrop to United's first month.

Romano also outlined that Carrick's confidence behind closed doors mirrors the tone he has struck publicly. "Carrick remains absolutely convinced too. What Carrick says in public – 'We are going to do very well, I am confident, this team is good' and all the rest – is what he's saying to the club.

"Carrick remains absolutely convinced that this team can do very well in the next weeks and months, especially after the break. So that's the feeling of Michael Carrick."

From a relaxed Manchester United fan perspective, this feels like the right call. It is far too early to start talking about sacking Carrick after four league games, especially when the club clearly appointed him with a longer-term idea in mind. If the board truly believed in him after last season, that belief should not disappear because of one bad month.

Supporters will not pretend the performances have been good enough. Four points from four games is poor, and losing at home to Manchester City always stings, whatever the circumstances. There is every right to question the level, the intensity and some of the in-game management. But there is also a difference between concern and panic.

The left-back issue stands out as something avoidable. If the club knew they needed one and failed to land the right player, that shortfall cannot be placed entirely on the manager. Carrick now has to find solutions with the group available, and that is part of the job, but recruitment and coaching are linked.

For now, the sensible view is to let this breathe. Carrick earned trust with what he did previously, and he deserves the chance to steady things after the international break. If results remain poor deeper into the season, the conversation changes. At this stage, patience feels smarter than noise.

articles.body:
Antonio Conte was last seen managing Serie A giants Napoli , where he also won the title two seasons ago. He is without a club right now and has expressed his views about a possible move to Turkey, with Manchester United also a possible option.

Tuttomercatoweb add background to the Italian's situation, noting that Fenerbahce have been interested in the ex-Tottenham manager.

But Conte isn't convinced about having Turkey as his next destination, as he awaits a top club. His stance has remained the same, even if the Italy national team also offered him a four-year deal.

A move to Manchester United could appeal to him, though. The outlet are sure he is on the Red Devils' shortlist, if they decide to part ways with Michael Carrick at some point in the season.

Juventus could also be a possible destination but they'd be less likely than Manchester United. He rejected a move to Turin in 2025 and there is little guarantee of that stance changing.
